## CEO overview

- **What is changing:** Codex Stop hooks now start background monitoring in a fully detached session and return within seconds instead of staying blocked until monitoring finishes.
- **Why it matters:** A blocked Stop hook left Codex turns hanging and could stall supervision when no monitor was already running.
- **Customer or business impact:** Codex sessions regain predictable turn endings, duplicate monitors are avoided when one is already healthy, and existing wake-queue and recovery behavior is preserved.
- **Risk and rollout:** Watcher startup timing and completion delivery are sensitive. The change stays within existing watcher, queue, and callback owners, adds executable regression coverage, and keeps bounded failure reporting rather than fire-and-forget behavior.

## What changed technically

- Route Codex Stop hooks through detached watcher arming so startup runs in a new session with inherited hook pipes and stdio closed, returns after bounded lock and beacon confirmation, and deduplicates when a healthy watcher is already running.
- Add launch and completion binding so identity-owned startup and failure records deliver queued wakes and startup failures through the existing home callback, including Codex secondmate launch notification exports.
- Add executable regression coverage for detached Stop behavior and wake-queue semantics, register the suites in the portable test runner, cap ShellCheck virtual memory with one invocation per lint root, and document the detached Stop contract in supervision and turn-end-guard docs.

## Validation

- **Checks passed:** Focused Codex Stop detach regression (10/10 hook-path cases with bounded timing and session or descriptor evidence), wake-queue Codex Stop semantics (9/9), portable parallel shard 1, lint with per-root ShellCheck and memory cap, and PR communication narrative. Prior pipeline intent, rebase, review, test, document, and push steps completed on this branch.
- **Checks not run:** Three real Codex CLI live scenarios remain blocked by account usage limits until Sep 15th 2026 8:24 AM.
- **Evidence and limitations:** Script regressions execute Firstmate hooks and watcher paths with simulated homes and processes; they prove orchestration behavior rather than live Codex CLI interpretation. Live e2e requires restored Codex quota and `FM_CODEX_STOP_DETACH_LIVE_E2E=1`. This narrative passes the local communication assessors when composed with the machine-owned Pipeline section.

## Module-boundary decision

Current module retained: detached Stop arming, launch confirmation, completion delivery, and wake-queue semantics remain in their existing watcher, arm, home-wake, spawn, and callback owners. No new adapter observer or broader control plane was introduced.

## Decision needed

No decision required.
